items.stem: A sentiment model labels 'not good at all' as positive. The most likely cause is:

options.text: The model mishandles negation and keys on the word 'good'
options.rationale: Correct: negation flips polarity and must be modelled.
Size is unrelated to negation handling.
Hardware does not cause this error.
Casing does not explain inverted polarity.

items.stem: For a dataset that is 95% 'not angry' and 5% 'angry', which TWO metrics are more informative than raw accuracy? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: recall shows how many angry tickets are caught.
Correct: F1 balances precision and recall on the rare class.
Accuracy is misleading when classes are imbalanced.

items.explanation: Correct: recall shows how many angry tickets are caught.

options.text: It is cheap, fast and often strong enough, setting a bar to beat
options.rationale: Correct: baselines quantify whether the transformer's cost is justified.
Not always; it is a baseline, not a guarantee.
They can and often do best.
